title: Opus 5.5 built my ingame intro scene and Im genuinely impressed
author: shurido
selftext:
I've been working on my game, Mineral Zone for around 9 months now and today Opus 5.5 built an in-game intro scene. (Voiceover via elevenlabs API)

And... I honestly didnt expect it to turn out this good.

I've been using AI heavily throughout development and somehow manage to burn through the limits of my €20 subscription almost every day since month. 😅

Mineral Zone is basically the game I've always wanted to play myself. It's a mix of tower defense, automation, resource gathering and base building. You build up your production, unlock new tech, expand your base and then try to survive increasingly difficult nights.

It also has multiplayer which was one of those features where I originally thought "Ill add that much later" and then somehow ended up building it anyway.

Im still doing the game design, deciding how everything should work, testing, tweaking and constantly throwing away things that dont feel right. But AI has made it possible for me to build something at a scale I absolutely never would have attempted alone.

This intro scene was one of those moments where I just sat there afterwards thinking:

"Okay this is actually pretty damn cool."

What you guys think about it?

Would you immediately notice that AI was heavily involved in creating this scene? Maybe the sounds need some improvement but the scene itself is pretty good i think. 

And for the other AI game devs here: have you had one of those moments yet where the result genuinely surprised you?

Btw im an Software Engineer full time and know how to code but unleashing my creativity with AI makes lots of fun!

Im searching for more beta testers, if you are interested DM me.

comments.author: track33r
comments.body: Did it come up with spaceship model too?

replies.author: shurido
replies.body: the small spaceship is an existing asset from my game. The big ship "Tessera" was fully generated during this run. The first iterration looked terrible but another run in Max-Mode did the job very well.

replies.author: track33r
replies.body: Wow, did it do it in Blender?

replies.author: shurido
replies.body: Kein Blender, wurde direkt im Code erzeugt

comments.author: Demintika
comments.body: Looks like Time Travel. I like Time Travel, please tell me more about the plot.

replies.author: shurido
replies.body:
Close! Its less time travel and more *parallel worlds*. You play a pilot sent to investigate a strange crystal on the planet Vesper. When it shatters the ship gets pulled through a rift into a version of the same planet. There an alien warden AI called VAEL, who lives across all these branches but has no body, drags you into a loop. She needs you to close the anomalies that keep tearing open and she pays you back with tech. You build factories and defences to hold each one, but there are infinitely many anomalies, so every mission is a new version of Vesper, and the question is what VAEL really wants from you. 

If you are interested in this type of game i can send you an beta key :)

replies.author: Demintika
replies.body: Thanks for the offer, but I am just interested in the plot for now. I will wait until you have a gameplay trailer / video before I try it.
